lots.what_it_is: Federation or early 1920s Australian Arts and Crafts blackwood (figured, possibly fiddleback) pedestal dressing table or duchess: two panelled cupboard pedestals with keyholes, two small central drawers below a low well, bevelled mirror between two panelled upstands, shaped aprons and block feet. Unmarked; maker unknown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: the form is a dressing table, not a sideboard (low central well with two drawers, small mirror set between upstands, pedestals at dressing height). Strong figure in the timber reads as blackwood, possibly fiddleback. Doors have keyholes but no pulls visible. Two drawers have small bar handles. Photo 2: square tapered legs with separate foot blocks, some look newer or reset; light wear and marks to the lower rails. No maker's mark or label visible in either photo; back and interior not shown. Photos are low resolution (800 x 600).
lots.condition: Appears sound and original in finish from the front; door pulls absent (keyholes only), foot blocks possibly replaced, minor wear to rails and edges. Back, drawer construction, mirror silvering and interior not shown.
lots.score_reason: An attractive Arts and Crafts design in figured blackwood, a cut above the run of 1940s blackwood dressing tables, but brown furniture is soft in Tasmania. Gowans blackwood dressing tables mostly hammer $50 to $200, with a Victorian mirror-back duchess at $270. A specialist dealer asks over $1,000 for restored Arts and Crafts blackwood, but that is retail and a different form. Likely hammer about $100 to $250.

lots.guide_summary: All six surviving Gowans results are SOLD hammers ($50 to $270) for blackwood or mirror-back dressing tables, but every one is a later or different style, so they are a category guide, not a same-item match. One dealer ASKING price ($1,295, Moonee Ponds Antiques, sideboard form) shows restored Arts and Crafts blackwood can retail high, but it is excluded from the range. No UNSOLD evidence. All AUD, no conversion; Gowans sale_price is in cents and is hammer only.
lots.working: No SOLD entry in the last 24 months is the same item: the researcher's sideboard results are a different form, and the Gowans dressing tables are later styles. So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For reference only, not a maximum: Tasmanian blackwood dressing tables have hammered $50 to $270 (all-in $61 to $329 at 22%).
lots.confidence_reason: The form and timber are clear from the photos, but there is no maker's mark and no same-item SOLD result. Search was capped and Carters, Antiques Reporter and Armitage past results could not be checked.

lots.question_for_armitage: Is this a dressing table (duchess) rather than a sideboard, and is it solid blackwood? Overall dimensions? Are the door pulls missing, and have the feet or foot blocks been replaced? Any maker's label or stamp on the back or in the drawers? Is the mirror silvering clear and does the mirror pivot?

lots.what_it_is: Large mixed lot of loose chandelier prisms and drops in several tubs and a bag: dozens of long faceted icicle prisms, many pear-shaped pendeloques, octagon button beads on wire, scalloped and kite-shaped plaques, spear drops, about 7 pink glass teardrop lustres, a few red drops, and a frosted glass bowl shade with chain. Cut or pressed glass, possibly some lead crystal; unmarked.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 shows the full spread: roughly 60 or more long prisms, 50 or more pendeloques and beads, plus tubs with more pieces not laid out, so the true count is hidden. Photo 2: pink glass teardrop lustres (7 seen), scalloped plaques, some brass wire hooks oxidised. Photo 3: long prisms show rainbow dispersion and sharp facets, which suggests decent quality cut glass or crystal, at least for some. Photo 4: pendeloques with old wire connectors; a few look cloudy or chipped. No maker marks (Swarovski style etching would not show at this resolution).
lots.condition: Used, loose and unsorted; wire connectors oxidised; some pieces may be chipped or cloudy. Contents of the closed tubs unknown.
lots.score_reason: Loose chandelier glass sells cheaply at Tasmanian auction: a small box of crystal drops made $25 and a box of long lustre prisms made $80 at Gowans. Lot 274 is bigger and more varied (pink lustres add a little), so perhaps $40 to $120 at auction. Retail per-piece prices on eBay and Etsy are only snippets and need hours of sorting and listing.

No UNSOLD evidence. eBay and Etsy ASKING prices of about AU$70 to AU$100 for small sets are snippet only and excluded from the range. All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = $25 (Gowans 416744, a smaller box, so a conservative floor); $25 / 1.22 = $20.49, round down = $20. Flip: likely resale about $80 (Gowans 374182 level, re-offered locally at auction); less about 20% seller's commission and costs ($16) and $0 postage = $64; $64 / 2.44 = $26.23, round down = $25. Both rest on close rather than identical lots, so treat them as soft ceilings.
lots.confidence_reason: Contents are partly hidden in tubs, glass versus lead crystal is unconfirmed, and the two SOLD results are close but smaller lots. Retail evidence is snippet only.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the Gowans 'BOX OF CHANDELIER PARTS' entry (lot ids 434799, 437541, 441175, 442760; $15 to $55): photos opened show brass arms, sockets and wiring, not glass prisms, so not the same kind (the researcher also flagged this). Dropped the US eBay/Etsy entry (https://www.ebay.com/itm/287561214372, US$129.99 and US$250): snippet only, eBay is closed to us, US retail, and the USD rate was assumed. The three remaining eBay AU and Etsy AU entries kept as unverified leads only.
lots.question_for_armitage: Roughly how many pieces are in the closed tubs, and is there any chipping or cloudiness? Are any pieces lead crystal or marked (for example Swarovski etched)? Does the frosted shade have chips?

lots.what_it_is: Jim Shore Heartwood Creek (Enesco) 'To All A Merry Night' Masterpiece Santa Sleigh, boxed: Santa in sleigh with toy sack and a team of flying reindeer on a rod over a winter village base with a large moon disc. Base has a knob at the right side, probably a wind-up music box or switch. Older retired piece; exact item number not read.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 1, 2 and 5: box front reads Jim Shore Heartwood Creek, 'To All A Merry Night', Masterpiece Santa Sleigh, matching the figure. Photo 2: knob or key at the right end of the base (music or light mechanism likely). Photo 3: close view of Santa, sleigh and first reindeer; paint looks clean, reins present; no breaks seen. Antlers on the upper reindeer appear intact at this resolution. Photo 4: Jim Shore biography panel on the box. No base stamp, item number or batteries compartment visible.
lots.condition: Appears complete and undamaged with its original box; mechanism working unknown; box shows light shelf wear. Reindeer antlers and reins are fragile and need checking.
lots.score_reason: A large, showy retired Jim Shore piece in its box. The only price found is Jim Shore's current US retail of US$235 for a different, newer LED musical sleigh, which shows these deluxe sleighs are not cheap new. Australian secondary demand for Jim Shore is thin and resale usually runs well below retail. Likely real value about $80 to $200, unproven.
